abstract: A 34-year-old woman presented to the rheumatology clinic with severe low back pain and arthralgia; later she developed bilateral knee pain and swelling, with limitation in ambulation and minimal improvement with nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs. Two weeks later she developed pain on the volar aspect of the right wrist and on the hypothenar region of the right hand. Examination showed swelling and tenderness of the right hypothenar region, tenderness and decreased flexion and extension of the right wrist, and bilateral knee effusions. The combination of arthritis and tenosynovitis raised the possibility of an ovarian tumor. A pelvic ultrasound revealed a complex, hyperechoic ovarian mass consistent with a cystic teratoma. Four weeks after removal of the teratoma, the polyarthritis and related symptoms resolved without therapy.
abstract_ja: 34歳女性が重度の腰痛と関節痛を主訴にリウマチ科を受診した。その後、両膝の疼痛と腫脹を生じ、非ステロイド性抗炎症薬による改善はわずかであった。2週間後には右手関節掌側と右手の小指球部に疼痛が出現した。診察では右小指球部の腫脹と圧痛、右手関節の屈曲・伸展制限、両膝関節の水腫を認めた。関節炎と腱鞘炎の併存から卵巣腫瘍の可能性が考えられた。骨盤超音波検査で、嚢胞性奇形腫に一致する複雑な高エコー性卵巣腫瘤が認められた。奇形腫摘出の4週間後、多発関節炎および関連症状は治療なしに消失した。
